selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main idea is taught in this passage about the One who runs the universe?
questions.answer: He is one and alone, and He takes care of everything in the universe.

questions.question: Besides the whole cosmos, what other levels are included in this order?
questions.answer: Its main supports, smaller parts, and all the beings inside it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the names and actions of Allah in the world?
questions.answer: They are active in a broad way and include everything or nearly everything.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention that many things are alike in nature and found in many places?
questions.answer: To show that one plan and one command are at work everywhere.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest by saying the same names and deeds appear in every place?
questions.answer: It suggests one Lord is acting everywhere.

questions.question: According to the passage, who is the ruler and caretaker of this kingdom?
questions.answer: The one and only Allah.

questions.question: Why is sharing rule between many gods rejected in this passage?
questions.answer: Because partners would bring conflict and disorder, not perfect order.

questions.question: Which relationships are denied for Him in the passage?
questions.answer: It denies that He has a partner, assistant, equal, or opposite.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is used in this section?
questions.answer: It reasons from the order in creation to the oneness of the Creator.

questions.question: What does the title “The Fifth Truth” introduce?
questions.answer: It introduces a new proof about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does “regularity” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means things happen in a steady, arranged, and consistent way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the universe as a whole and its smaller parts?
questions.answer: Both the whole universe and its smaller parts show the same organized care.

questions.question: How are the Divine Names and actions described in relation to all things?
questions.answer: They are said to surround and include all things or most things.

questions.question: What does the passage say these signs “demand” or strongly require us to accept?
questions.answer: That the One who made and manages everything is one and without partner.

questions.question: What does the passage clearly deny about Allah’s rule?
questions.answer: It denies any partner, helper, equal, rival, weakness, or defect.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah compared with all others?
questions.answer: It teaches that He is one, unique, and alone, with no equal.

questions.question: What bad results are linked with claiming partners for Allah?
questions.answer: Disagreement and disorder.

questions.question: How does this passage help strengthen iman for a young Muslim reader?
questions.answer: It teaches that when we look at the world’s order, we can recognize Allah’s oneness more clearly.

questions.question: What quality of the cosmos is mentioned first in this passage?
questions.answer: Its complete order and regularity.

questions.question: How are the beings in the universe linked to one another?
questions.answer: They are connected as parts of one shared plan.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Divine Names and actions at work in the world?
questions.answer: They reach across everything or almost everything, not just one small part.

questions.question: How are the Divine Names and deeds working in the world described?
questions.answer: They work through everything widely and in a way that covers all or most things.

questions.question: What do those images help us understand?
questions.answer: They help us understand that the universe is run in an organized and planned way.

questions.question: What does the passage say order shows by itself?
questions.answer: Order itself points to one organizer.
